Bring a breath of the French countryside into your kitchen with this gorgeous set of three botanical wall art prints — and honestly, this is one of my favourite picks for kitchen art wall decor right now. Each print features a softly rendered botanical study — open poppy blooms with delicate buds and stems, a tall sprig of berry-laden eucalyptus, and a graceful leafy branch — all rendered in deep charcoal and gentle mid-grey tones against a warm ivory background. There's a quiet, pressed-flower quality to each one that feels both timeless and completely at home in a rustic or cottage kitchen.

I love how the palette works — the ivory ground keeps things light and airy, while the grey botanical illustrations add just enough depth to feel considered rather than plain. If your kitchen leans French Country, Scandi-rustic, or classic cottage, these three prints will slot right in. They're calm without being boring, and the trio hangs together beautifully as a set.

How to Style Kitchen Art Wall Decor in a French Country or Cottage Kitchen

I'd hang all three prints in a row at eye level, with an equal gap between each — around 5 to 8 cm works nicely and keeps things neat without looking rigid. Above a dining table, a dresser, or a stretch of blank wall beside your kitchen cabinets are all brilliant spots. Because the ivory and grey palette is so versatile, these prints sit beautifully against white, warm cream, soft sage, or even a muted dusty blue wall. They're the kind of prints that quietly tie a room together without demanding attention.

If you'd like to mix them into a gallery wall, pair them with other botanical or nature-inspired pieces in similar neutral tones — linen textures, wicker, and natural wood accessories will really complement the rustic, country feel. For more ideas on building a kitchen gallery wall, have a browse through our botanical wall art collection — there are plenty of pieces that work alongside this set perfectly.

Choosing the Right Size and Finish for Your Space

Before you choose a size, it's worth standing in front of the wall where you plan to hang these and getting a rough sense of the width available. As a general guide, all three prints side by side should span roughly two-thirds of the wall width — that gives the set visual weight without overcrowding the space. In a smaller kitchen or on a narrow wall, smaller sizes feel just right and keep things neat; in a bigger open-plan kitchen-diner, you can go larger and really let the botanicals make a statement.

For finish, Luster art paper gives you a slight sheen that makes the ivory and grey tones pop beautifully in natural light — a great all-rounder. Museum quality paper has a smoother, more matte finish that suits a more refined, gallery-style look if that's the feel you're going for. Both options print the charcoal and grey tones with lovely depth and clarity. aiItems.content:
What is kitchen art wall decor?

Kitchen art wall decor refers to prints, paintings, or illustrated artworks chosen specifically to hang in a kitchen or kitchen-diner space, adding personality, colour, and warmth to what is often a purely functional room. It can range from botanical prints and food-inspired illustrations to typographic quotes and abstract designs — anything that makes the kitchen feel more like a curated, lived-in home. In recent years, French Country and botanical styles have become especially popular choices, thanks to their timeless, relaxed quality that suits both traditional and contemporary kitchens. A well-chosen set of kitchen art wall decor can completely change the feel of the room, making it a more welcoming place to cook, eat, and gather. Sets of three prints are a particularly popular format because they create an instant, balanced gallery-wall look without the guesswork of curating individual pieces.

How to Hang Kitchen Art Wall Decor: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure the space: Find a clear stretch of wall — above a dining table, beside the cooker, or along a run of cabinets works well. Measure the width so you know how much room you have for all three prints side by side.

2. Decide on the layout before you hang: Lay all three prints out on the floor first and adjust the spacing until it looks right — usually 5 to 8 cm between each print is a good starting point. Take a photo so you can refer to it when you're up the ladder.

3. Find the right height: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level — around 145 to 155 cm from the floor is the standard guide. If you're hanging them above a piece of furniture, aim for 15 to 20 cm above the top of the furniture.

4. Mark and hang: Use a pencil to lightly mark where each hook or nail will go, double-check with a spirit level, and then hang the prints. Step back and adjust any that need a small nudge.

5. Style around them: Once they're up, bring in complementary textures — linen, wood, wicker, or a small potted herb — to tie the botanical, French Country feel together.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Our Kitchen Art Wall Decor Formats

Unframed Print — You receive the art print only, ready for you to pop into a frame of your choice. Great if you already have frames or want to match a very specific existing decor. Available in Luster art paper (slight sheen, vibrant tones) or Museum quality paper (smooth, matte, gallery-style finish).

Framed Print — The print comes already mounted and framed, ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saver and ideal if you want a polished, finished look immediately. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper finishes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped tightly around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary, borderless look. Arrives ready to hang. No glass, no frame — just clean, textured botanical art on the wall. Available in a range of canvas size options.

aiItems.content:
What are paintings in living room?

Paintings in living room refers to wall art prints or artworks displayed in a living space to add personality, colour and style to the room. They are one of the most popular and affordable ways to decorate a home, instantly transforming a plain wall into a focal point. Sets of prints — like a coordinated trio — are especially popular because they create a curated, gallery-style look without requiring any design expertise. From bold abstract canvases to soft botanical studies like this French Country set, there is truly a style to suit every taste and interior scheme.

How to Hang Paintings in Living Room: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and anchor point: Identify the wall you want to fill — above the sofa, a fireplace or a console table are all excellent spots. Measure the width of the space so you know how much room you have for all three prints side by side.

2. Plan your layout before you hang: Lay the three prints on the floor in front of the wall first. Decide on the gap between each piece — 5 to 8 cm is a good rule of thumb for a neat, balanced look. Mark the spacing lightly with a pencil on the wall.

3. Find the right hanging height: The centre of your arrangement should sit at roughly eye level — around 145 to 150 cm from the floor is the standard guide. If the prints will hang above furniture, aim for 15 to 20 cm above the top of the sofa or console.

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable when you have three prints in a row. Use a spirit level or a level app on your phone to keep everything perfectly straight before you put any nails or hooks in.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back to the opposite side of the room and check the overall effect. Small adjustments now are much easier than rehanging everything later — take your time and enjoy the process!

Choosing Your Format: Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas?

Finish — Unframed print: print only, ready for you to frame as you choose. Framed print: arrives complete and ready to hang. Wrapped canvas: image printed on canvas stretched over a wooden frame, no additional framing needed.

Paper / Material — Unframed print: available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: printed on canvas material.

Ready to hang? — Unframed print: no — you will need to source your own frame. Framed print: yes — saves you the time and cost of finding a frame. Wrapped canvas: yes — arrives ready to display straight away.

Best for — Unframed print: those who already have a frame or prefer a specific frame style. Framed print: those who want a complete, polished look with minimal effort. Wrapped canvas: those who prefer a contemporary, frameless look with real depth and texture.

Suits this botanical set? — Unframed print: great if you want to choose your own frame colour. Framed print: the easiest way to get a gallery-wall look quickly. Wrapped canvas: adds a tactile, artisan quality that suits the botanical subject beautifully.
